raw_response:
I farm only 2 mu, so every bag of fertilizer and every trip for spraying matters. I will still follow the wheat-maize routine I know, because changing too much on a small plot is risky. What I do first is look at what worked for me and the other people around Quzhou County last year, then adjust a little. Since I have well irrigation, I will not save too hard on water at the key stages. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put the base fertilizer down a bit heavier, and make sure the water goes on at overwintering, jointing, and filling if the soil is dry. Wheat here cannot be starved, or the ears stay small. After wheat harvest, I will turn straight to maize and use hybrid seed, because the hybrids around here usually give steadier yield. For maize I will put nitrogen a bit higher than wheat, because if maize loses vigor in summer it is hard to pull it back. I would rather spend a little more on fertilizer than lose grain. On my small land, I can manage the work myself, so I will keep to rotary tillage, 2 spray rounds on each crop, and water when the crop is really asking for it.
